value: acoustic startle response as the first response to AHD exposure in four of six tagged porpoises
eye: ear; whole-animal behavioural response (acoustic startle) of free-ranging tagged porpoises
method: tagged free-ranging exposure to an acoustic harassment device, received level measured on the animal, startle detected in tag movement data
conditions: Free-ranging harbour porpoises in Danish waters: six juveniles (2 F, 4 M; Table 1) incidentally trapped in pound nets set by local fishermen (tagged May 2018, September 2019, October 2019), tagged within 24 h of discovery, handled on a boat for at most 19 min (mean 9 min), fitted with suction-cup DTAGs (sound, 3D movement, plus GPS in n = 3 or ECG in n = 2) and released; exposure began 16 to 202 min after release with the animals free-swimming at sea. Stimulus: a commercial Loftech acoustic harassment device playing 500 ms 14 kHz pulses (harmonics at 28 and 42 kHz) at random intervals of 0.6 to 90 s for 15 min; source level 189 dB re 1 µPa rms at 1 m. Received level measured on the animal's tag (band-passed 10-46 kHz): initial RL per animal (Table 1) HP1 130, HP2 131, HP3 132, HP4 98, HP5 99, HP6 106 dB re 1 µPa rms-fast (125 ms); the Discussion gives 96 dB for HP5 and the Results 102 dB for HP4's first ping (mean 99 dB of five first pings); HP5's RL came from pings among the first 34 because of low signal-to-noise. Initial range printed only for the GPS animals (HP1 0.9, HP3 2.2, HP5 6.9 km); the abstract gives 0.9-7 km. Control: the 15 min immediately before each exposure as baseline; a separate drone-observed experiment on untagged porpoises used control playbacks with pings reduced by 80 dB. The authors say recent tagging may have affected cardiac responses in HP1 and HP2 (exposed 16-17 min after release) and read the untagged trial as evidence that flight was not caused by tagging-induced sensitisation. Startle (jerk within 0.2 s of first ping) in four animals (HP1-HP3, HP6); HP4 and HP5, the two lowest received levels, did not startle; five of six (HP1-HP3, HP5, HP6) increased distance to the source; HP4 neither fled nor fed and made a deep quiet U-shaped dive.
